newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia may tell offices to buy "national" car.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia may tell offices to buy "national" car.

text.p: An Indonesian minister has indicated government organisations might soon have to buy a "national car" produced by a firm controlled by one of President Suharto's sons to boost sales, newspapers reported on Wednesday.

The Jakarta Post quoted Trade and Industry Minister Tunky Ariwibowo as telling reporters on Tuesday compulsory purchases were needed to help sales of the Timor car, which have slumped despite favourable tax and tariff breaks.
Japan, the United States and the European Union have complained to the World Trade Organisation (WTO) over the national car policy, saying it discriminated against other manufacturers.

The government last year gave PT Timor Putra Nasional, a company controlled by President Suharto's youngest son Hutomo Mandala Putra, tax and tariff breaks to produce the sedan car in association with South Korea's Kia Motors Corp.

The Jakarta Post said the company had expected to sell more than 3,000 cars in February, but according to statistics released by the country's largest car maker, PT Astra International, it managed to sell only 962.
This was down from 3,259 in January, the paper said.
"What's important to me is that the product is sold and the national programme runs well. That's my responsibility," Tunky was quoted as saying.
He said the government would not set any targets for Timor sedan purchases by government offices and state companies, adding that details would be announced soon.

Tunky said last week Jakarta had scheduled talks with Japan, the United States, and the European Union (EU) over the car policy. Indonesia has said the programme was aimed at strengthening its domestic industry.
Indonesia on May 23 blocked a request by the EU to set up a dispute settlement panel to look into whether the national car project violated internation trade regulations.
